newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end 2.11 pct down on fund sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end 2.11 pct down on fund sales.

text.p: Thai stocks tumbled for the fourth straight day, retreating another 2.11 percent on Friday on sustained active sales by foreign funds, brokers said.
The SET Index fell 21.65 points to 1,004.89 on moderate 7.2 billion baht turnover. Losers overwhelmed winners 251 to 89.
The index lost a combined 94.12 points, or 8.6 percent, since Tuesday with banks and finance firms bearing the brunt of the week's heavy setback.
"Market sentiment was hit by heavy foreign selling. Small investors hope the market support fund would be active again next week," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of Sitca Investment and Securities.

Somchai referred to a 15.7 billion baht fund set up by private commercial banks and brokerage firms to shore up batter Thai stocks in early September. The fund has not been active in the last few weeks.
Chetta Meemangkang of Prime Finance and Securities said foreigners sold bank and finance blue-chips, probably as part of a shift of their Thai investment to neighbouring countries.

"Worries about weak third quarter earnings coming out from late this month, and doubt about stability of a new Thai government to be formed after general elections, prompted the sell-off today," Somchai said.
Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa last Friday dissolved parliament and called snap elections on November 17.
Brokers said investors were concerned that the new elected coalition government would not enjoy stability.

Most major sectors retreated on Friday with the transport counter leading the decline, falling 3.51 percent, followed by the finance sector shedding 3.15 percent, and communications issues losing 3.09 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, falling six baht to 204. The biggest Thai bank said on Friday it was considering to raise deposit rates by about 25 basis points soon.
Finance One lost three baht to 92.50, and debuting Hipro Electronics ended six baht lower than its 32-baht IPO.
